summary: Edward H. Schafer worked in sinology. He studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley (B.A.), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (M.A.), and Harvard University (Ph.D.). He served in UC Berkeley's Department of Oriental Languages (~1947–1984) and as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward H. Spieker was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and other fields. He attended Baltimore City College and earned his A.B. (1877–1879) and Ph.D. (~1877–1882) at Johns Hopkins University, where he served as Associate Professor of Greek and Latin from 1880 to 1918.

Edward Hamilton Johnston specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. After attending Eton College, he studied at New College, Oxford, and under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1924) and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit and a Balliol College Fellow in 1937.

Edward Henry Palmer worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Sayyid Abdallah and at St John's College (~1863–1867), later serving as Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from 1871 to 1881.
Edward Hincks worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He received his education at Midleton College and Trinity College Dublin, graduating with a B.A. (1807–1812).

Edward James Rapson worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at St John's College under Cecil Bendall and Edward Byles Cowell, later holding professorships of Sanskrit at University College London (1903–1906) and the University of Cambridge (1906–1936).

Edward John Thompson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After schooling at Kingswood School and Richmond College, he taught English at Bankura Christian College (from 1910), lectured in Bengali at Oxford (1923), and was a Research Fellow in Indian History at Oriel College (1936–1940).

Edward Joseph Thomas worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under John Burnet at the University of St Andrews and at Emmanuel College, Cambridge. He worked at Cambridge University Library (~1909–1950), serving as Head of the Oriental Languages Department (1909–1940).

Edward Kamens specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University (~1970–1982) and later served on its faculty from 1986 to 2022 as Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

Edward Klich worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Jagiellonian University (~1898–1902) under Jan Michał Rozwadowski and became a professor at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań in 1929.
Edward Lavallin Puxley was active in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Brasenose College in 1852 and served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from 1859 to 1866.

Edward Lucas Hogarth was a scholar in Indology. He earned his B.A. and M.A. at Brasenose College (1859), taught Sanskrit at the University of Oxford, and served as Head Master of the Government Provincial School, Calicut.
Edward Payson Newton worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Princeton University from ~1866 to 1870 and subsequently attended Pittsburgh Theological Seminary from ~1870 to 1873.

Edward Peter Rice worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Cheshunt College (~1869–1873) and the University of London (B.A., ~1870–1873), and served with the London Missionary Society from 1873 to 1915.

Edward Rehatsek worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied civil engineering at Eötvös Loránd University, served as Professor of Mathematics and Latin at Wilson College, Mumbai (~1847–1871), and was an examiner at the University of Mumbai (1869–1881).

Edward Ross works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and religious studies. He studied at McGill University (BA), the University of Hong Kong (MBuddhStud), and the University of Reading (PhD, 2020–2024), where he was an Associate Lecturer from 2020 to 2025.
Edward Russell Ayrton worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After attending St Paul's School, he studied under Flinders Petrie (~1902–1904) and held a post at Abydos (~1902–1904).

Edward S. Casey works in philosophy. He studied at Yale, Northwestern (Ph.D.), and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at Yale (~1967–1978), served as dean of philosophy at Stony Brook (~1978), and was president of the American Philosophical Association (2009–2010).

Edward Sapir worked in linguistics. He studied under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt, earning his B.A. and Ph.D. at Columbia. He headed the Geological Survey of Canada's Division of Anthropology (1910–1925) and held professorships at the University of Chicago and Yale University.
Edward Thomas was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College (~1830–1832) and served as a writer in the Bengal Civil Service from 1832 to 1857.
